sections.h2: Which Louisville offices value and bill a Jefferson County house?
sections.html:
The PVA sets the value and the Sheriff sends the bill. The Sheriff's own description says it gathers about $1 billion a year from over 300,000 taxpayers for 13 taxing jurisdictions, among them the state, Louisville Metro, the school board and several fire districts.

The PVA works from the Glassworks Building, 815 W. Market St., Suite 400, Louisville, KY 40202, phone (502) 574-6380. The Sheriff's Property Tax Department is inside the Fiscal Court Building at 700 W. Liberty St., phone (502) 574-5479, with counter hours of 8 AM to 4 PM on weekdays.

Assessments track fair cash value on January 1. A bill goes to the owner of record on that date unless the PVA had already posted the new owner before the roll was printed.

sections.h2: What is the Jefferson County payment calendar?
sections.html:
Bills are mailed by November 1, and the 2 percent discount here runs through December 1, a month longer than the November 1 date written into state law. After that the stages step up on this Sheriff's calendar.

Payment stages posted by the Jefferson County Sheriff for the current-year tax bill (source: Jefferson County Sheriff's Office)
DatesAmount owed
November 1 to December 1Bill less 2 percent
December 2 to January 4Bill at face value
January 5 to February 5Face value plus 5 percent
February 6 to April 15Face value plus a 10 percent penalty and a 10 percent Sheriff's add-on fee

A due date that falls on a weekend or a Sheriff's Office holiday slides to the next working day. Not getting a bill does not excuse a late fee, so call the department if nothing has shown up by the second week of November.

  • At the counter, use cash, a check or a money order with your payment stub.
  • By mail, send a check to Jefferson County Sheriff, PO Box 34570, Louisville, KY 40232-4570.
  • Online, an eCheck costs $2 and a card costs 2.25 percent, or a flat $1.95 on payments of $86 or less.
  • Dropboxes sit at the downtown office and at County Clerk branches such as Dixie, Fairdale, Highview, East and Westport.

Partial payments on a current bill are welcome during these months.

sections.h2: Can I contest the value the PVA put on my Louisville house?
sections.html:
Yes, and the process begins with a PVA conference, not a board hearing. KRS 133.120 requires it during the yearly open inspection period, and Jefferson County runs it through an online form.

  • File one conference per parcel ID.
  • Attach an appraisal, photographs, an insurance policy, repair quotes, construction costs or a listing agreement.
  • Pick comparable sales from about the last two years, matched on size and type. The PVA opens its sales search to the public free for the appeal window.
  • Look for a written result in 5 to 10 business days.

Still unhappy? Sign the lower portion of the result form and hand it to the Jefferson County Clerk by one workday after the inspection period closes. The Local Board of Assessment Appeals takes it from there, and an owner who bypasses that board loses access to the Board of Tax Appeals. Paid representatives need written authorization and must fit a listed profession.

Filing does not freeze the bill. You pay on the value you claimed, and any shortfall plus interest arrives later if the board lands higher.

sections.h2: How much can the homestead exemption cut a Jefferson County bill?
sections.html:
For 2025 and 2026 it removes $49,100 from the assessment of an eligible owner's home. Owners must be 65 or older, or totally disabled, and live in the house.

Take the $248,400 Census value for a typical owned home here. After the deduction, the taxable base is $199,300. The exemption shrinks a bill and cannot erase it unless the assessment is smaller than the deduction. File through the PVA with a birth certificate, driver's license or passport, and for disability, proof of benefits from a federal or retirement-system program.

West End homeowners may have another option. LHOME and the West End Opportunity Partnership offer a grant or 0 percent loan toward the residential bill in nine neighborhoods: Algonquin, California, Chickasaw, Park DuValle, Parkhill, Parkland, Portland, Russell and Shawnee. LHOME's number is (502) 882-8091.

sections.h2: Does a small city inside Jefferson County send its own bill?
sections.html:
Frequently. The Sheriff's bill funds the state, Metro, schools and fire districts, while many smaller cities inside the county bill their own residents on top.

The PVA tallies 83 incorporated taxing jurisdictions among roughly 60,000 properties. Those cities offer services such as police, sanitation and parks, and each sets its own rate. State law has recognized just two city classes since 2015: first class, which is Louisville, and home rule cities, which are all the rest.

A seller in a place like St. Matthews or Jeffersontown should call city hall for a balance and a payoff letter. Looking only at the Sheriff's account can miss a separate city liability.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid Jefferson County tax when the house sells?
sections.html:
The debt stays with both owner and land. Under KRS 134.015 it counts as the taxpayer's personal obligation from the assessment date, and the KRS 134.420 lien can last 11 years whoever holds title.

A bill unpaid on April 15 moves to the Clerk. Interest of 1 percent per month and added fees follow, and a third party can buy the certificate at the summer sale. The County Attorney's page estimates the extra cost near 40 percent once the certificate is created.

A payment plan with the County Attorney blocks the sale of that bill, though plans for a given year open only after the Sheriff's collection period closes. Written requests for certain penalty waivers go to the same office.

At the closing table, the Sheriff explains, the seller typically pays a prorated share for the months owned and the buyer then covers the full bill when it comes. Check the settlement statement to see how your closing agent divided it.

sections.h2: How big is the Jefferson County housing market?
sections.html:
This is Kentucky's most populous county, with 795,222 residents in the Census Bureau's 2025 estimate and a boundary shared with Louisville Metro. It spans 380.8 square miles of land, about 2,056 people per square mile in 2020.

  • Typical value of an owned home, 2020 to 2024: $248,400.
  • Share of homes lived in by their owners: 62.1 percent.
  • Monthly owner costs: $1,593 with a mortgage and $608 without.
  • Median household income: $69,866.
  • Housing units in 2025: 366,702.

Children attend Jefferson County Public Schools, or the Anchorage Independent district through eighth grade. Questions about recording a deed go to the County Clerk's Legal Records Division.

faqs.q: Where can I hand in a Jefferson County tax payment?
faqs.a: At the Sheriff's office, 700 W. Liberty St., Louisville, by mail to PO Box 34570, online or in a dropbox. Counter hours are 8 AM to 4 PM on weekdays, and the counter takes cash, checks and money orders.

faqs.q: How long does the 2 percent early discount last?
faqs.a: It lasts from November 1 through December 1. Face value applies from December 2 to January 4, and the 5 percent charge starts January 5.

faqs.q: Will the Sheriff take part of a bill now and the rest later?
faqs.a: Yes, on current-year bills while collection is open, from November 1 to April 15. Once a bill moves to the Clerk, eligibility for a payment plan is decided by the County Attorney.

faqs.q: When must I challenge a value I think is too high?
faqs.a: During the open inspection period each year, through the PVA's online conference. A board appeal through the Clerk follows only if the conference fails, and tax bills themselves cannot be contested.

faqs.q: Does closing on the sale wipe out a tax lien?
faqs.a: It does not. A lien survives a change of owner, and the title company will insist on payment from your proceeds. Get a figure from the Sheriff for the current year and from the Clerk for anything older.
